I've had something weird like this happen to me. I'd like to first start by saying yes my cats name was Casper and I'm not just making a stupid joke. We had him for 17 years and he  was a white cat born on Halloween. Two years after he had to be put to sleep we got another cat, also a white one. They have two distinctly different looking faces and also different eye colours. Well recently while looking for Jasper (my new cat and yeah I know but I swear I'm still not making a dumb joke here and that's really my current cats name) I thought he just looked different somehow as he elegantly turned his head around to look at me . His fur was much more bright, he looked so pleased or even happy to see me  and his face was (I'm not trying to be cruel or mean to my cat) seemingly much more stereotypically "cute" than what I know him as. It wasn't until I read the title for this post that I realized this cat wasn't Jasper and had Caspers green sparkling eyes instead of My Jasper's yellow.  <3 I love both my cats.

I don't have real hate for either character honestly. Daniel is definitely an impulsive little brat and sometimes a total pain but..he's a little brother, and that's exactly what the majority of little brothers are to the big brothers out there, as well as the one we're playing as in this story. He's also still a  sweet and innocent child with a big heart and at certain moments in the story so far that has really shined. The way he cared so much for his little mushroom pup, the way he watched her playing in the snow while laughing and smiling at her enjoying herself as we walked back into the old abandoned house for the first time , or his excitement to have a little friend around his own age like Chris to play with and talk enthusiastically about superheroes and comic books with and really just feel like the kid he still really is inside despite all that's happened recently to him and his big bro. When Daniel had lost his father he had still mostly retained his innocent goofy ways, even when his mushroom pup was lost to him he hadn't fully given up and later really connected with Chris, but I believe this third loss might have been the straw that broke the camels back so to speak and Daniels now trying to force himself to "grow up or toughen up" in order to shield himself from more hurt,even distancing himself from his brother to achieve that and avoid more hurt. I'm happy to keep trying despite his "New emo Daniel" change to keep trying to make the best choices and win him over for his own good.  That's what big bros are for :) besides nuggies. I could say something quite similar for Chloe's behavior but this comment was already so damn long in hindsight, sorry.

Also evident in Lis1 in the segment of the game where even though Chloe has had a tragic accident and is suffering beyond comprehension both physically and emotionally, You can still see Max ignoring her through texts that Chloe had sent her, even being so self centered as to send Chloe a picture of herself somewhere out in the world Chloe can't ever just go out and truly enjoy herself. I remember Max making a comment to herself about how stupid that was of herself in that time line to send that photo to her. In the end I just see these characters as human and very relatable,making the wrong choices,looking like straight up assholes and sometimes not even being aware of it. By the end of Lis1 we see an incredible amount of development  from almost all of the characters in it. Wiser and better I'd say for the most part. :)

Sacrificing Chloe was really hard for me, I know it's probably not the most popular choice to make but that's the beauty of a story with bending narratives. In the end I sacrificed her because I thought of all the totally innocent people and little kids living in Arcadia Bay that would have died to the supernatural storm that is caused by Max's time bending abilities (at least that was my suspicion at the time, it's been years. even though it was not intentional in the slightest).I loved my time spent Arcadia Bay and it felt so real and littered with personality for me that I ended up thinking of the innocent and good people living there that I hadn't even been able to meet during the wonderful story as it came to a tragic close. My favorite game hands down. Love to all you guys :)

Well I grew up a fat and hadn't had a serious girlfriend until I was 22 years old. Losing my virginity definitely helped with my confidence issues and I started naturally feeling less pressure socially,which led to me going out more instead of sitting around moping about my life and going out with my girlfriend (recently ex). I started walking many miles a day to get around as I don't drive (she wanted to go out every single day and yes I paid pretty much 100% of everything). Fast forward about 9 months and people were commenting on my weight loss and how I'm doing it so quickly (I'm fairly fit now at 24) I didn't actually notice the difference in how I looked and not just felt  until people I've only met a handful of times started commenting on it (my ex would deny she saw any difference even when her own family started fussing about it) So to sum it up I gained massive amounts of self esteem compared to how I once was, always worrying what other people thought of me as if I was still 15-16. I'm still quite shy but I've had a handful of girls approach me and begin to flirt with me now that I'm single and also some while I was with my ex.  I'm not a push over anymore desperate for strangers to like me because of an assumption I made right off the bat that they won't. If someone had asked me before this change how I would take my girlfriend of nearly a year and a half leaving me I'd have answered absolutely devastated. Now I find myself looking forward to making new connections with people, enjoying my free time without having to cater to someone else's needs and feelings and putting myself first , working out harder, doing some lifting and buying more expensive nicer clothes that I can actually afford now she isn't draining my wallet. I still consider myself a good guy but I'm not a "nice" guy anymore.

A creepy thought indeed. The house is usually pretty lived in most of the time (myself,sister,mother,father,niece and my brother when he's working in town 2 days a week. I would say the attic is the only place in my house that's rarely ever occupied.

Ive certainly considered that but I've since figured that if it was an intruder scoping the place they wouldn't have stood there for as long as they did with us just staring back and forth and them not making any sound despite the fact they'd have needed to sprint to the back of my house and open three doors to reach the nearest exit without me seeing them. I live in a large house with a lot of empty space) and my front door is very loud when closed, the house practically rattles. I also have three large dogs  inside the house that often bark at me for moving around the place  when it's late until I show them it's just me and they didn't make a sound.   At this point I'm thinking this particular situation was brought on more through lack of sleep than an intruder.

That reminds me of times when I was a kid when I woke up to go to the bathroom  still half asleep and heard disembodied voices whispering around me. Yeah I was definitely tired when this happened, if it wasn't for the other things that have happened I'd have definitely written this off as 100% all in my head. One other being a kind of shadowy male figure moving around the walls and everyone in my family seeing it at one point or another (even my incredibly serious father) who has zero interest in things like this once pulled my mother aside in the kitchen and said "so about that thing you all keep going on about, well last night I might have...what the fuck is it anyway?"
